title: The elderly
hookLine: Francis called grandparents the memory of a people
tomorrow: who is lonely, just one phone call away from you?

lines: BEFORE IT WAS A PHONE SHOP.
cards: Somebody's grandmother remembers what the corner store sold before it was a phone shop, the song everyone danced to at her wedding, and which cousin was named for whom. So what do grandparents carry that nobody else can?
Pope Francis gave it a name. He called grandparents the memory of a people. Not a museum, but a living memory, the kind that only works if someone younger sits down and asks.

teach.h: RISE UP BEFORE THE HOARY HEAD.
teach.b: Scripture puts the old at the center. In Leviticus, the command is physical, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man." Stand up when they come in.

teach.h: OLD MEN DREAM, YOUNG MEN SEE.
teach.b: The prophet Joel pictures a day when God's spirit is poured out on everyone, and gives the old and the young two different jobs: "your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions."
Francis took up that pairing in his letter to young people. The old dream, he said, and the young take those dreams and turn them into vision. Neither works alone.
The Church even honors a pair of grandparents.
Tradition, not the Gospels, names Mary's parents Joachim and Anne, and Catholics keep their feast together, the grandparents of Jesus.
In Luke, the ones in the Temple who recognize the child are two old ones, Simeon and Anna, who had waited and watched.
Francis warned against a throwaway culture that treats the old as finished. In this tradition, they hold the stories that tell a family, a parish, a street who it is.
Lose them unheard, and the people forgets itself. That's why a visit to an old person isn't only charity. It's how memory gets passed on.

how: Catholics celebrate Saints Joachim and Anne, by tradition Jesus's grandparents, and the Church now keeps a World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly; parishes bring Communion to elderly people who can't come to Mass.

o: anyone who has retired from full-time work
people the Church excuses from fasting
the old, who carry what a family remembers

games.q: the old at the center — tap the pairs.

old men dream, young men see visions

s: the Gospels give the names of Mary's parents
Joachim and Anne come from tradition, not the Gospels.
Leviticus tells people to stand up before the aged
in Joel, only the young receive God's spirit
the old dream dreams and the young see visions: both.

games.q: your grandfather keeps telling the same story about the day he arrived in this country. your cousins roll their eyes. what fits?
o: ask him a new question about that day.
gently remind him he's told it before.
record it once so he doesn't have to repeat it.
games.why: a living memory works when someone younger asks. a recording keeps the words; a question keeps the man in the story.

practice: Find one thing an older person gave you or left you: a photo, a ring, a recipe card, a rosary, a voice message. Hold it, or picture it, and look at it closely for the sit. What story comes with it that only they could tell?
Think of one older person you could visit or call this week, and one question you'd like to ask them.

wordCard.voice: The elderly. The people who carry what a family remembers, and dream the dreams the young turn into vision. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, Leviticus 19:32 in the Vulgate: rise up before the white head.

carryVoice: Your line: the memory of a people. It lives only while someone asks. See you tomorrow.
